previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and homelessness presented with worsening numbness and pain in her lower extremities after spending multiple nights on the street. She was diagnosed with mild (first-degree) frostbite of the right foot, likely due to cold exposure, and was managed with pain control, wound care, and tetanus prophylaxis. Vascular surgery recommended no surgical intervention. A urine culture showed only yeast, consistent with colonization rather than bacterial infection, so she was treated with a short course of fluconazole and discontinued from antibiotics to avoid resistance. She also had a stage II pressure ulcer on her heel and chronic pain related to her spinal injury. Despite recommendations for discharge to a shelter with nursing support or visiting nurse services, she insisted on going to a friend’s house and was discharged with wound care instructions, pain medications, and close follow-up advice. Her condition was stable at discharge.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old woman with right toe frostbite and right flank pain.

1. suspected UTI vs chronic colonization, however a urine 
culture was not sent in the ED prior to antibiotics.  They did 
not change her foley catheter.  A specimen was obtained after 
foley change on the floor after antibiotics in the ED, and grew 
mixed flora.  I have requested that the nurse here on the floor 
change the catheter and obtain a fresh urine specimen for 
culture.  She had no signs or symptoms of infection, as she was 
afebrile and had no leukocytosis.  Antibiotics were held and she 
left AMA.

2. frostbite, second degree -- rewarming, wound care.  Ibuprofen 
to decrease cytokine release.  Vascular surgery evaluated in a 
previous admission and felt no surgical plan was indicated.  At 
this point, it appears she might lose part of her first hallux, 
but the demarcation of dead tissue remains to be seen.

3. polysubstance abuse/homelessness -- social work consult for 
resource/rehab options.
.
4. paraparesis/wheelchair bound/urinary retention -- decubitus 
precautions, pt has been previously advised to follow up with 
urology for discussion of a suprapubic catheter.
.
5. gram positive rod bacteremia -- presumed skin contaminant, 
was not treated.  As I write this discharge summary, I see a 
second culture is now positive, but she has left AMA.
.
Ms. ___ eloped without telling staff at 8AM on ___.  
Security was called, as she still had a femoral central venous 
catheter in place, but she was not located.  I have placed a 
safety alert about placing central lines in this patient, as she 
gets them in the ED for access, but in my experience has never 
been hemodynamically stable.  Unless it is clear she needs IV 
antibiotics, it would be better for her safety if she did not 
have central lines, as she does leave AMA frequently.
